proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted joint global causal-optimizer inference under pointwise exchangeability and an estimated Gelbrich constraint, but random-diagonal potential-outcome lifts invalidated the causal identification and positive transfer claims. Repairs preserved the original full-data target and established full [0,1] ambiguity, unique antipodal quadratic optimizers, the exact honest localization frontier 2 rho_0 (1-alpha_CI), and matched risk order kappa + N^(-1/2). The math review passed, but the field novelty gate failed; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: The frozen consistency and pointwise exchangeability conditions do not identify the literal fresh-draw causal mean for a continuously distributed exposure, even with bounded, jointly measurable potential-outcome evaluation. One observed law admits every constant causal value in \([0,1]\), and two shape-qualified lifts of that same law have unique antipodal causal optimizers, each with exact global quadratic growth. Any globally honest optimizer region must have expected outer localization error at least \(2\rho_0(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{CI}})\) on these experiments. Thus the obstruction persists without competing branches or higher-order minima and with positive curvature at each fixed positive amplitude. The matched full-model joint-loss order remains \(\kappa+N^{-1/2}\), with elbow \(\kappa\asymp N^{-1/2}\). The proposed causal Gaussian transfer and shrinking joint confidence construction fail; observed score algebra and deterministic normal transport remain supporting results.
gap: Huang et al. compares causal mixture shifts on a population Gelbrich equality surface and supplies finite-tilt inference and stationary search. Regular causal-optimizer and estimated-constraint results require invertible reduced curvature. Generic set inversion, uncertain-budget bounds, and resource calibration are established, but the inspected literature does not verify attainable joint inference on this learned nonlinear surface or the stated two-sample joint loss.
fill: The formal kernel links a primitive learner class to a derivative-uniform Gaussian and multiplier theorem, complete normal transport, ambient whole-set coverage, and a same-class matching calibration consequence. The novel amplitude envelope and localized gradient dominance enter only the risk class; curvature-free coverage uses the base class. The open localization frontier must respect global branch competition and possible covariance cancellation.
